newsitem.title: LEBANON: Lebanon's banking activity up in September.
newsitem.headline: Lebanon's banking activity up in September.

text.p: The consolidated balance sheet of Lebanon's commercial banks rose 1.4 percent in September to 33,353 billion Lebanese pounds, the Bank of Lebanon said in its latest monthly bulletin.
Total deposits in foreign currencies and Lebanese pounds rose 1.17 percent to 27,663 billion pounds from 27,342 billion in August, it said.
Lebanese pound deposits grew 3.74 percent to 11,664 billion pounds from 11,243 billion a month earlier.
Deposits in foreign currencies fell 0.40 percent to $10.266 billion in September compared with $10.307 billion in August, the Bank added.
Dollarisation of bank deposits dropped to 57.84 percent from August's 58.88 percent. The dollarisation rate stood at 67.97 percent at the end of September 1995.
Loans and credits to the private sector rose 1.53 percent in September over August, increasing to 11,955 billion pounds.
Credits in Lebanese pounds fell 3.45 percent in September to 1,532 billion from 1,587 billion pounds in August.
Credits in foreign currencies rose 2.54 percent to $6.687 billion from $6.522 billion.
Dollarisation of credits rose to 87.11 percent from 86.52 percent at the end of August, the Bank said.
